claims.text: The as-produced Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The as-produced alloy has a fairly homogeneous elemental distribution.
The additive manufacturing process leaves residual stresses in the alloy.
Changing oxygen partial pressure at elevated temperature alters the formation and stability of the surface oxide scale.
Moderately oxidizing conditions produce a continuous, adherent Al/Cr-rich oxide scale.
A continuous, adherent Al/Cr-rich oxide scale slows further degradation of the underlying fcc matrix.
Reducing conditions make the protective scale discontinuous or poorly adherent.
Excessively oxidative conditions make the protective scale discontinuous or poorly adherent.
Loss of scale integrity permits internal oxidation and elemental depletion.
Internal oxidation and elemental depletion increase intergranular stresses.
Increased intergranular stresses facilitate crack initiation and propagation.
Rapid crack propagation can cause catastrophic failure.
Specimens exposed to optimal oxidizing conditions will degrade more slowly than specimens exposed to reducing or overly oxidative conditions.
Reducing or overly oxidative exposure will produce accelerated internal oxidation and embrittlement.
Reducing or overly oxidative exposure will cause greater strength loss and crack formation than optimal oxidizing exposure.
The proposed degradation behavior is expected above approximately 700 °C.
Significantly lower temperatures or near-inert atmospheres may not trigger the same degradation mechanism.
The as-manufactured alloy lacks a significant oxide scale before elevated-temperature gas exposure.
